title: Retry bounded parallel drain with config and schema landing together
summary: Retry job 20261016-200605-xh54: the drain runs independent items of one plan group concurrently, up to a new [parallel] max_concurrency (default 1). The Config field is added in config.rs in the same change as the athena.toml section, and a test parses the real athena.toml. The audience is the Athena user running a drain, who wants a shorter wall time and unchanged serial behavior by default.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust and TOML.
New drain and config tests; cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt --check pass.
Criteria check concurrency with a barrier test, not just the presence of a field.
Schema and config land in one change, with a test that loads the real athena.toml.
Multi-job `athena go` and the --pr phase stay out of scope.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
A test enforces that the real athena.toml parses under Config.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The typed request, 'try again', takes precedence over the introspection's proposed repair/guard job. This retry rebuilds the parallel drain; it does not build the commit-time config check.
The repository I see (the base) has no [parallel] in athena.toml and no parallel field in Config (grep found neither), so it parses today. Nothing needs repairing first.

The earlier failure was the athena.toml edit landing without the schema field. Here the schema field and the athena.toml section go in one change, and a test parses the real athena.toml to prove they match.

Send+Sync bounds on traits in gh.rs and jev.rs, plus admission.rs test fixes (the test used [parallel] as an unknown section), are likely needed and should be listed this time, as should README and roles-and-ladder wording.
A panic in a worker is documented as not isolated (as in the earlier attempt), unless it is cheap to isolate.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test loads the repository's real athena.toml (with its [parallel] section) through Config and passes. A config without [parallel] yields max_concurrency 1. A config with an unknown top-level section is rejected. Run `cargo test`.
A drain test with bound 1 shows items run strictly in the existing order, and all existing drain tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A drain test with bound 2 and two independent items in one group has both in flight at once (barrier; fails if serial). An item that depends on another starts only after it finishes. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
Tests show one item's failure or refusal does not stop its siblings, the worker bound is never exceeded, and Stop starts no further item. Run `cargo test`.
Ordering and retry rules are unchanged; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

The [parallel] section in athena.toml and its schema field in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs are in the same change. The field, its default (1) and its ceiling are documented where defined. The final report names and justifies the athena.toml change.

The Drain and Report docs no longer say the loop runs one job at a time. docs/design/parallel-jobs.md and CHANGELOG.md state what this slice built and what remains (multi-job `athena go`, the --pr phase), and disclose the Send+Sync trait changes.

out_of_scope: A commit-time or submit-time config/schema consistency check (the introspection's proposal).
Isolating worker panics per item, unless it is trivial.
Rewording the '(could run in parallel)' plan-groups label in display.rs.
departures: The change is larger than the reference median: concurrency in the drain plus trait bounds across crates. The prior attempt failed at the gate, so the cost and pass estimates are adjusted.
